subject: physics
note: One revision note per concept. Each GCSE spec point is primary in exactly one concept; non-primary refs are broad points that also need this note.

concepts.title: Units, prefixes and standard form
concepts.scope: SI units, prefixes from giga to nano, converting units (e.g. hours to seconds), significant figures and standard form in physics calculations.
concepts.data_note: taught by AQA (units and maths-skills appendix) but no matching spec point

concepts.title: Energy stores and systems
concepts.scope: The energy stores, the ways energy is transferred between them, conservation of energy in a closed system and energy transfer diagrams.

concepts.title: Kinetic and gravitational potential energy
concepts.scope: Calculating kinetic energy (½mv²) and gravitational potential energy (mgh) and the energy changes between them, e.g. a falling object.

concepts.title: Work done
concepts.scope: Work done as energy transferred by a force (W = Fd), the joule as a newton-metre, and work done against friction causing heating.

concepts.title: Power
concepts.scope: Power as the rate of energy transfer or work done (P = E/t, P = W/t) and the watt as one joule per second.

concepts.title: Energy dissipation
concepts.scope: How energy is dissipated (wasted) into less useful stores, usually by heating the surroundings, in every system change.

concepts.title: Reducing unwanted energy transfers
concepts.scope: Reducing wasted energy with lubrication, thermal insulation and low-resistance wires, and how wall thickness and thermal conductivity affect a building's rate of cooling.

concepts.title: Efficiency
concepts.scope: Calculating efficiency as useful output over total input energy or power, and ways to increase efficiency.

concepts.title: Energy resources
concepts.scope: Renewable and non-renewable energy resources, their uses, reliability and environmental impact, and trends in their use.

concepts.title: Circuit symbols and measuring current and potential difference
concepts.scope: Standard circuit symbols, drawing circuit diagrams, and connecting ammeters in series and voltmeters in parallel to measure and test circuits.

concepts.title: Charge and current
concepts.scope: Current as the rate of flow of charge (Q = It), conditions needed for current to flow, and current being the same everywhere in a single loop.

concepts.title: Potential difference, current and resistance
concepts.scope: How current depends on potential difference and resistance (V = IR) and how a variable resistor changes current.

concepts.title: I–V characteristics, thermistors and LDRs
concepts.scope: I–V graphs for a fixed resistor, filament lamp and diode, ohmic versus non-ohmic components, and how thermistor and LDR resistance changes with temperature and light.

concepts.title: Required practical: resistance and I–V characteristics
concepts.scope: Building circuits to investigate how resistance depends on wire length or combinations of resistors, and to plot I–V characteristics of components.

concepts.title: Series and parallel circuits
concepts.scope: Rules for current, potential difference and resistance in series and parallel circuits, and calculating equivalent resistance.

concepts.title: Direct and alternating current
concepts.scope: The difference between d.c. and a.c., and the UK mains supply of 230 V at 50 Hz.

concepts.title: Mains electricity and plug safety
concepts.scope: Live, neutral and earth wires, their potential differences, fuses, circuit breakers and why touching the live wire is dangerous.

concepts.title: Electrical power and the heating effect of current
concepts.scope: Electrical power (P = IV, P = I²R, P = E/t) and the heating effect of a current explained by electron–lattice collisions.

concepts.title: Energy transfers in everyday appliances
concepts.scope: Energy transferred by appliances (E = Pt, E = QV), potential difference as energy per unit charge, and power ratings of household devices.

concepts.title: The National Grid
concepts.scope: How the National Grid uses step-up and step-down transformers and high-voltage transmission to reduce energy losses.

concepts.title: Static electricity
concepts.scope: Charging insulators by friction through electron transfer, attraction and repulsion of charges, sparking, earthing and everyday uses and dangers of static.

concepts.title: Electric fields
concepts.scope: Electric fields around charged objects and between parallel plates, field-line diagrams and how fields explain static effects.

concepts.title: States of matter and density
concepts.scope: The particle model of solids, liquids and gases and calculating density (ρ = m/V), including why the states differ in density.

concepts.title: Required practical: density
concepts.scope: Measuring the density of regular and irregular solids and of liquids using mass, dimensions and displacement.
concepts.data_note: taught by OCR (PAG practical activity) but no matching spec point

concepts.title: Changes of state
concepts.scope: Melting, freezing, boiling, evaporating, condensing and sublimating as reversible physical changes in which mass is conserved.

concepts.title: Internal energy
concepts.scope: Internal energy as the total kinetic and potential energy of the particles, and how heating raises temperature or changes state.

concepts.title: Specific heat capacity
concepts.scope: Specific heat capacity and calculating the energy needed to change temperature (ΔE = mcΔθ).

concepts.title: Specific latent heat
concepts.scope: Latent heat of fusion and vaporisation, calculating energy for a change of state (E = mL) and heating and cooling curves.

concepts.title: Required practical: specific heat capacity
concepts.scope: Determining the specific heat capacity of water or a metal block and obtaining a heating curve for melting ice.
concepts.data_note: taught by OCR (PAG practical activity) but no matching spec point

concepts.title: Gas temperature, pressure and absolute zero
concepts.scope: How the motion of gas particles relates to temperature and pressure, absolute zero and converting between kelvin and Celsius.

concepts.title: Gas pressure, volume and doing work on a gas
concepts.scope: Pressure acting at right angles to surfaces, pV = constant at fixed temperature, and why doing work on a gas (e.g. a bicycle pump) raises its temperature.

concepts.title: Structure of the atom
concepts.scope: The nucleus of protons and neutrons with orbiting electrons, the size of atoms, relative masses and charges, energy levels, ions and absorption or emission of radiation.

concepts.title: Atomic number, mass number and isotopes
concepts.scope: Atomic and mass numbers, nuclear notation and isotopes as atoms with different numbers of neutrons.

concepts.title: Development of the atomic model
concepts.scope: How the model changed from the plum pudding model through Rutherford's alpha scattering experiment to Bohr and the discovery of the neutron.

concepts.title: Radioactive decay and nuclear radiation
concepts.scope: Alpha, beta, gamma and neutron emission, their nature, penetration and ionising power, activity in becquerels and detection with a Geiger–Müller tube.

concepts.title: Nuclear equations
concepts.scope: Writing and balancing nuclear equations for alpha, beta-minus, beta-plus and gamma decay and their effect on atomic and mass number.

concepts.title: Half-life
concepts.scope: The random nature of decay, half-life from graphs and data, and calculating net decline after a number of half-lives.

concepts.title: Background radiation
concepts.scope: Natural and man-made sources of background radiation and how dose depends on location and occupation.

concepts.title: Contamination, irradiation and radiation hazards
concepts.scope: The difference between contamination and irradiation, how hazards depend on radiation type and half-life, and safety precautions.

concepts.title: Uses of nuclear radiation
concepts.scope: Medical and everyday uses of radiation, including tracers, PET scans, radiotherapy, smoke alarms and sterilisation.

concepts.title: Nuclear fission
concepts.scope: Fission of uranium-235, chain reactions, control rods and moderators in a reactor, and the pros and cons of nuclear power.

concepts.title: Nuclear fusion
concepts.scope: Fusion of light nuclei with release of energy, why it needs very high temperature and pressure, and the difficulty of fusion power.

concepts.title: Scalars and vectors
concepts.scope: Scalar and vector quantities such as distance and displacement, speed and velocity, and representing vectors as arrows.

concepts.title: Contact and non-contact forces
concepts.scope: Contact and non-contact forces and how forces arise from interactions between pairs of objects.

concepts.title: Weight, mass and gravitational field strength
concepts.scope: Weight as the force of gravity (W = mg), measuring weight, free-fall acceleration and how g differs on other planets.

concepts.title: Resultant forces and free body diagrams
concepts.scope: Finding resultant forces, free body diagrams, resolving forces and equilibrium using scale vector diagrams.

concepts.title: Forces and elasticity
concepts.scope: Elastic and inelastic deformation, Hooke's law (F = ke), linear and non-linear force–extension graphs and work done stretching a spring (½ke²).

concepts.title: Required practical: force and extension of a spring
concepts.scope: Investigating the relationship between force and extension for a spring and the work done in stretching it.
concepts.data_note: taught by OCR (PAG practical activity) but no matching spec point

concepts.title: Moments, levers and gears
concepts.scope: The moment of a force (M = Fd), the principle of moments, and how levers and gears transmit turning effects.

concepts.title: Pressure and pressure in liquids
concepts.scope: Pressure as force per unit area (p = F/A) and how pressure in a liquid depends on depth and density (p = hρg).

concepts.title: Upthrust and floating
concepts.scope: Why objects in a fluid feel upthrust equal to the weight of fluid displaced, and what decides whether they float or sink.

concepts.title: Atmospheric pressure
concepts.scope: A simple model of the atmosphere and why atmospheric pressure decreases with height.

concepts.title: Speed, velocity and distance–time graphs
concepts.scope: Distance, displacement, speed and velocity, s = d/t, average speed, measuring speed in the lab, and reading speed from distance–time graphs.

concepts.title: Acceleration and velocity–time graphs
concepts.scope: Acceleration (a = Δv/t), the equation v² − u² = 2as, and finding acceleration and distance from velocity–time graphs.

concepts.title: Typical speeds and accelerations
concepts.scope: Typical everyday speeds for walking, cycling, cars, wind and sound, and estimating everyday accelerations compared with g.

concepts.title: Newton's first law
concepts.scope: How an object stays at rest or at constant velocity unless a resultant force acts on it.

concepts.title: Newton's second law and inertia
concepts.scope: Resultant force, mass and acceleration (F = ma), and inertia and inertial mass as resistance to changing velocity.

concepts.title: Required practical: force, mass and acceleration
concepts.scope: Investigating how the acceleration of a trolley depends on resultant force and on mass, using light gates or timing.
concepts.data_note: taught by OCR (PAG practical activity) but no matching spec point

concepts.title: Newton's third law
concepts.scope: Equal and opposite force pairs acting on different objects, in equilibrium and in collisions.

concepts.title: Circular motion
concepts.scope: Why an object moving in a circle at constant speed has a changing velocity and needs a centripetal force.

concepts.title: Stopping distance and reaction time
concepts.scope: Thinking plus braking distance, factors that affect each, measuring reaction times and how stopping distance varies with speed.

concepts.title: Braking forces and large decelerations
concepts.scope: Work done by brakes, braking distance depending on speed squared, and estimating the forces and dangers of large decelerations on the road.

concepts.title: Momentum and conservation of momentum
concepts.scope: Momentum (p = mv) and conservation of momentum in collisions and explosions.

concepts.title: Changes in momentum and safety features
concepts.scope: Force as rate of change of momentum (F = mΔv/Δt) and how air bags, seat belts and crash mats reduce force.

concepts.title: Transverse and longitudinal waves
concepts.scope: Waves transferring energy without matter, the difference between transverse and longitudinal waves, and evidence from ripples and sound.

concepts.title: Wave properties and the wave equation
concepts.scope: Amplitude, wavelength, frequency and period, and calculating wave speed (v = fλ, T = 1/f).

concepts.title: Required practical: measuring wave speed
concepts.scope: Measuring the speed, frequency and wavelength of waves in a ripple tank, on a string and of sound in air.
concepts.data_note: taught by OCR (PAG practical activity) but no matching spec point

concepts.title: Reflection of waves
concepts.scope: Reflection, absorption and transmission at boundaries, the law of reflection, specular and diffuse reflection, ray diagrams and total internal reflection.

concepts.title: Refraction
concepts.scope: How waves change speed and direction at a boundary, wavefront diagrams, and how absorption, transmission and refraction vary with wavelength.

concepts.title: Required practical: refraction of light
concepts.scope: Investigating refraction of light through rectangular glass blocks by tracing rays and measuring angles.
concepts.data_note: taught by OCR (PAG practical activity) but no matching spec point

concepts.title: Sound waves and hearing
concepts.scope: How sound travels through solids, how the ear converts sound to vibrations, the limited range of human hearing and changes when sound enters a new medium.

concepts.title: Ultrasound, infrasound and seismic waves
concepts.scope: Using ultrasound echoes for imaging and sonar, seismic P and S waves for exploring the Earth's core, and calculating distance from echo times.

concepts.title: The electromagnetic spectrum
concepts.scope: EM waves as transverse waves with the same speed in a vacuum, the order of the spectrum, and visible light as the only part we can see.

concepts.title: Uses of electromagnetic waves
concepts.scope: Practical uses of each part of the spectrum, and how radio waves are produced by and induce oscillations in circuits.

concepts.title: Dangers of electromagnetic radiation
concepts.scope: How the danger of EM radiation rises with frequency, the harmful effects of microwaves, infrared, UV, X-rays and gamma, and radiation dose.

concepts.title: Lenses
concepts.scope: Converging and diverging lenses, focal length and lens power, ray diagrams, real and virtual images and magnification.

concepts.title: Visible light and colour
concepts.scope: How the colour of objects and filters depends on differential reflection, absorption and transmission of wavelengths.

concepts.title: Black body radiation
concepts.scope: How all bodies emit and absorb infrared, perfect black bodies, the balance of absorbed and emitted radiation and the Earth's temperature.

concepts.title: Required practical: infrared radiation and surfaces
concepts.scope: Investigating how the nature of a surface affects how much infrared it emits or absorbs, e.g. with a Leslie cube.

concepts.title: Magnets and magnetic materials
concepts.scope: Magnetic poles, attraction and repulsion, magnetic materials and the difference between permanent and induced magnets.

concepts.title: Magnetic fields
concepts.scope: Magnetic field lines around bar magnets and uniform fields, plotting compasses and evidence that the Earth has a magnetic core.

concepts.title: Electromagnetism and solenoids
concepts.scope: The magnetic field around a current-carrying wire and a solenoid, the right-hand grip rule and electromagnets.

concepts.title: The motor effect
concepts.scope: The force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field, Fleming's left-hand rule and F = BIL.

concepts.title: Electric motors and loudspeakers
concepts.scope: How the motor effect makes a coil rotate in an electric motor and makes a loudspeaker cone vibrate.

concepts.title: Electromagnetic induction
concepts.scope: Inducing a potential difference by moving a conductor relative to a magnetic field and the factors affecting its size and direction.

concepts.title: Generators and microphones
concepts.scope: How alternators produce a.c., dynamos produce d.c., and microphones turn sound into electrical signals using the generator effect.

concepts.title: Transformers
concepts.scope: How transformers change alternating voltage, the turns ratio equation Vp/Vs = Np/Ns and VpIp = VsIs.

concepts.title: The Solar System
concepts.scope: The Sun, planets, moons and dwarf planets, how the Sun formed from a nebula, and how models of the Solar System changed over time.

concepts.title: Life cycle of stars
concepts.scope: How stars like the Sun and more massive stars evolve from nebula to white dwarf, neutron star or black hole, and the balance of gravity and fusion.

concepts.title: Orbits and satellites
concepts.scope: How gravity keeps planets, moons and satellites in circular orbits with changing velocity but constant speed, and how orbit radius depends on speed.

concepts.title: Red-shift and the expanding Universe
concepts.scope: The Doppler effect, red-shift of light from distant galaxies and why it shows the Universe is expanding.

concepts.title: The Big Bang and Steady State theories
concepts.scope: Comparing the Big Bang and Steady State models and the evidence from red-shift and cosmic microwave background radiation.

concepts.title: Observing the Universe
concepts.scope: How telescopes and observation methods have changed and why some telescopes are placed in space.
